text:
maya_support: FYI customer AcmeCorp (INC-4721) reports repeated partial SSE fragments after client reconnects when traffic passes through their gRPC-web gateway. They see truncated last event and then reconnects produce duplicate prefix tokens.

acme_infra: Confirmed. Happens only when requests route via our gRPC-web reverse proxy -> converts HTTP/2 upstream to HTTP/1.1. Direct calls to hosted API (h2 end-to-end) look fine.

samir_eng: Can you paste a short curl/replicator that shows the behavior? Also any error lines from the gateway or our edge?

acme_infra: Repro steps (simplified):
```
# client (browser -> gRPC-web proxy)
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  --http1.1 "https://gw.acme.internal/v1/stream?model=redwood-13b" 
```
Observed: stream starts, emits tokens, then around 18s: connection resets, client reconnects, new stream starts but first ~200 bytes of next stream are duplicate of previous end. Final application gets duplicate prefix + missing trailer.
```
# our edge log sample (redacted)
[2025-11-12T15:23:18Z] INFO connection=abcd stream=12 sent_event len=182
[2025-11-12T15:23:36Z] WARN connection=abcd stream=12 upstream-reset reason=RST_STREAM code=2
[2025-11-12T15:23:36Z] INFO connection=abcd stream=13 downstream-reconnect
[2025-11-12T15:23:36Z] DEBUG stream=13 replayed_prefix_len=198
```

jon_oncall: Thanks. Two likely culprits: 1) intermediary is buffering and slicing chunk boundaries differently when translating H2 DATA frames -> H1 chunked encoding, and then client reconnect logic re-sends part of buffered data. 2) trailers (or missing end-of-stream marker) get dropped during conversion, so the gateway closes early and then next connection sees leftover bytes.

maya_support: Customer also reported auth errors intermittently before the drop (401), then a reconnect succeeds. Could be token refresh race + gateway retrying the request mid-stream. Any billing impact? They said some sessions count as two partial requests.

samir_eng: If gateway retries a request because of a 401, and the runtime had already emitted N tokens, the gateway might be replaying buffered output while issuing a second downstream request; the client then receives duplicate prefix. That explains duplicate + missing suffix. Billing wise we are charged for both partial streams; ops will need to reconcile.

acme_infra: We dumped a tcpflow around the moment of failure. I can share a hex of the last 512 bytes if helpful. There are HTTP/1.1 chunk sizes repeated and a stray "0\r\n" missing before the final CRLF.

samir_eng: Please run the repro with these quick checks to narrow it down:
- produce an h2->h1 pass-through using nghttpx/nginx with http2 on upstream and http1 on downstream and capture with tcpdump.
- try curl with --http2-prior-knowledge directly against our edge and against the gateway.
- enable proxy debug for "preserve-traillers"/"send-trailers" flags.

Suggested commands:
```
nghttp -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --method GET https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-13b
# on gateway host
tcpdump -s0 -w /tmp/dump.pcap port 443 and host <edge-ip>
```

infra-bot: Escalation created -> INC-4721-ESCL, assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P2.

jon_oncall: Hypothesis tests: 1) If you reproduce but set the gateway to not buffer (flush every chunk), does duplicate prefix go away? 2) If you force the client to reconnect with a cache-busting header (x-reconnect: 1) do we still see suffix loss? 3) Try enabling keep-alive on the downstream connection to see if connection reuse masks the split.

acme_infra: Quick test results: disabling buffering reduced duplicate prefix frequency but didn't eliminate it. Forcing reconnect still sometimes leaves missing trailing tokens.

samir_eng: Sounds like a trailer/end-of-stream detection bug in the proxy. Two paths forward:
- Short term: Recommend the customer enable direct HTTP/2 end-to-end for streaming (if possible) or enable gateway setting "passthrough_streaming": true so it proxies raw frames rather than re-chunking.
- Long term: Eng-runtime to add stricter EoS checks and a validation layer that ensures we don't acknowledge downstream completion until upstream trailers/0-length chunk confirmed. Also add dedupe protection when a client reconnects within X ms of a prior stream from same session id.

maya_support: I've sent the immediate mitigation steps to Acme (point them at the passthrough flag + a curl example) and asked them to attach a tcpdump when they see it next. I've also requested billing hold pending investigation.

jon_oncall: For eng-runtime: can you add a debug hook to log when a stream is proxied from h2->h1 and whether a trailer was present/stripped. Log fields: upstream_eos, downstream_eos, trailer_present, buffered_chunk_count. That will make root cause easier.

samir_eng: Will do. I'll open a repo ticket and draft a tiny patch to gate trailing logic. In the meantime, ops: please mark billing for INC-4721 as disputed until we confirm double-charge.

acme_infra: Appreciate it. If we can get a recommended nginx/nghttpx config snippet that preserves trailers, that would help.

maya_support: Adding that to the playbook now. Will follow up when eng has the logs and a patch. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INC-4721-ESCL updated -> status: investigating, owner: samir_eng, sla: 72h
